summary: Verified (a) wholesaler 'Place Order on Their Behalf' modal and POST /api/wholesaler/{wid}/orders, (b) GET /api/wholesaler/{wid}/distributors/{did}/detail surfaces newly-placed orders, and (c) GET /api/allocation/kpis + the new Performance KPI strip on /manufacturer/allocation. Backend: 5/6 pytest pass; 1 failure exposes a real tenant-scoping bug (a distributor user can call /api/allocation/kpis and receive Unilever's KPIs — HTTP 200 instead of 403). Frontend: both Place-Order modal flow and Allocation KPI strip render and behave per the spec.

critical.issue: Tenant-scope bypass. A distributor caller (lagos.distributor@tradekonekt.io) gets HTTP 200 with the parent manufacturer's KPIs (fill_rate 65%, requested 37935, etc). Root cause: routes/allocation.py::_scope_manufacturer (line 54) accepts any role with `user.manufacturer_id` or `user.organization_id` populated — distributor user records carry the parent manufacturer_id and silently pass. The same helper guards /allocation/pool, /allocation/summary, /allocation/recommendation, /allocation/decisions, /allocation/orders/* — so the leak is broader than /kpis. Fix: add an explicit role allowlist (e.g., allow only role in {'manufacturer','super_admin'}; warehouse role with explicit org scope) BEFORE returning mfr id.

action_items: FIX backend: harden _scope_manufacturer in /app/backend/routes/allocation.py to reject non-manufacturer (and non-super_admin) roles. Currently distributor + wholesaler + retailer can all read manufacturer allocation data because their user record carries the parent manufacturer_id.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/allocation.py is 812 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. New KPI block (~190-360) is a natural extraction candidate (allocation_kpis.py).

_scope_manufacturer is the single line of defense for ~12 endpoints and trusts a per-user `manufacturer_id` field that is populated for downstream roles. Add a role allowlist and unit test for each non-manufacturer role explicitly.

allocation_kpis loads up to 5000 orders, 10000 allocations, 5000 fulfillments and computes in Python. For a real tenant this scales O(n) per request — consider a Mongo aggregation pipeline ($group on status + $lookup to order_allocations) to push the math server-side.
_parse_iso silently swallows ISO parse errors — log a warning so silently-bad timestamps don't get excluded from KPI windows.

Service-Level uses delivered_at OR dispatched_at as the completion timestamp. Dispatched is not the same as delivered; either compute two metrics or always require delivered_at to be present for 'completed' orders.

Warehouse on-time uses fulfillment_orders.updated_at as the proxy for the SLA stop-clock — updated_at can be mutated by any later status change. Prefer a dedicated `delivered_at` field on fulfillment_orders.
EB001 lint warning in allocation.py force_back_order remains (pre-existing, not from this change — confirmed in spec).

rca of the issue: Bug: GET /api/allocation/kpis (and ~11 other allocation endpoints) leak manufacturer KPI data to distributor callers. Repro: POST /api/auth/login {email:'lagos.distributor@tradekonekt.io',password:'TradeKonekt2026!'} → use the access_token to GET /api/allocation/kpis?days=30 → 200 with Unilever's fill rate, units, warehouse leaderboard, etc. Root cause: routes/allocation.py::_scope_manufacturer (lines 54-65) checks only `if user.role == 'super_admin'`, then returns `user.manufacturer_id or user.organization_id` without a role allowlist. Distributor user records carry the parent manufacturer_id (used elsewhere for catalog/tenant scoping), so the helper happily returns Unilever's mfr id and every downstream query is scoped correctly to the leaking tenant. Mitigation: insert a role check immediately after the super_admin branch — `if user.get('role') not in {'manufacturer','warehouse'}: raise HTTPException(403, 'Manufacturer scope required')` — and add pytest coverage for each non-manufacturer role per endpoint.
